identity.name: Submariner
identity.one_liner: The no-date Submariner produced 1962-1989 — the longest-running Sub reference and the staple of vintage Rolex collecting.

provenance_events.description: The 5513 runs 1962-1989 — the longest-running no-date Submariner reference, and the watch most associated with the British Ministry of Defence issue Submariners of the 1970s.

The 5513 runs 1962-1989 — the longest-running no-date Submariner reference, and the watch most associated with the British Ministry of Defence issue Submariners of the 1970s. The Hong Kong vintage market trades 5513s heavily.

narrative.story: The 5513 ran nearly three decades on calibers 1530 and 1520, spanning gilt gloss dials, matte dials with painted markers, and finally gloss dials with white-gold surrounds. That length of production created a catalog of collectible variants — 'Bart Simpson' coronets, meters-first depth text, serif dials — and a price ladder that runs from entry-vintage to six figures for early gilt examples. Roger Moore wore a modified 5513 in Live and Let Die.
narrative.collector_notes: Dial originality first: service dials with modern lume are common and cut value hard. Match the dial era to the serial, check bezel-insert correctness, and expect unpolished cases to command large premiums.
